#1657. Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea

The stirring of what might yet be a great partnership between Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, although it will need to be, given some of the chaos that endures at Chelsea.

This was a Premier League game played at a furious pace, and the two former Real Madrid team-mates in charge of the sides will not have seen much of the control all coaches seek. Xabi Alonso’s team eventually won with a goal from each of his attacking triumvirate of Rogers, Palmer and João Pedro – and at times it will have been painful for the new Chelsea manager.

That was chiefly the fault of Robert Sánchez, who was embraced afterwards by Alonso, having demonstrated just how damaging a shaky goalkeeper can be to any serious team. Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham had their moments – and the best ones were granted to them by Sánchez. At a club that is such a restless trader of footballers, it feels remarkable that Sánchez has endured for so long.

Alonso played down the significance of Sánchez’s errors, although he cannot seriously be considering sticking to his mantra of “relax and carry on”. That was, he said, his response to the first-half Sánchez mistake that let in Josh King’s shot for Fulham’s first goal. Sánchez could have done a lot better with Gonzalo García’s goal after the break.

Fulham have equalised against Chelsea thanks to Josh King's low strike 💥 pic.twitter.com/WCLKB7XqeE

Gonzalo Garcia has scored on his Premier League debut after Robert Sanchez spilled Castagne's shot 🤯 pic.twitter.com/BmP6eqwkuN

Chelsea have a lot of faith that Mike Penders, the 21-year-old Belgian on the bench for this game, will be their first-choice goalkeeper eventually. The situation seems rather more urgent and with Penders likely to feature against Luton Town on Thursday night in the Carabao Cup it would appear a big decision is looming for Alonso.

In terms of the Palmer-Rogers axis, this was very promising, although there was no doubting the senior figure in this. Palmer’s ball set João Pedro free in the first minute, the Brazilian lifting a well-judged nudge over Bernd Leno.

"A flying start under Xabi Alonso!" Chelsea lead against Fulham after just 31 seconds 🤯 pic.twitter.com/LrkYxOReFB

It was Palmer who was crucial to the second for Rogers, made by Maxence Lacroix on his debut. Palmer stroked in the third on 49 minutes with the easy confidence of a man in form.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

"Cole Palmer back to his best!"Palmer has scored to double Chelsea's lead! 🥶 pic.twitter.com/zo6e0Vdcgq

“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

“We concede goals in the first minute, the end of the first half and the beginning of the second half and there are not worse moments to concede. But we showed character and personality and I am very proud of how my players responded. We deserved a little bit more but football is not about what you deserve, it is about what you take. If you lose against a team like Chelsea they [should] have to do a little bit more. For me, they are easy goals for them and mistakes we cannot make. We need to improve and be more ready in the first minute, that is for sure.

“We are on our way and we will keep improving. The first thing I want to see is a competitive team. We were tonight, we tried our best and tried to play our football against a team like Chelsea, which is not easy. I believe in them and I believe in young players. I think they have the energy and ambition I want and they fit in the way I play. Josh King is absolutely amazing. I am really happy with him. Gonzalo [Garcia] scored and Cesar [Palacios] did well. I think they need a bit more time but they are doing great and making an impact already.”

The final whistle is blown at Craven Cottage and Chelsea hold on to win 3-2 to give Xabi Alonso a win in his first game in charge. Alvaro Arbeloa’s first game as Fulham boss ends in defeat. An absorbing west London derby.

Garcia throws himself to the ground as Sessegnon sends in a cross but that is never going to be a penalty.

Will there be one more chance for Fulham to try and find an equaliser? Time is running out for the hosts.

Pedro has the ball in the back of the Fulham net but Quenda was offside in the build-up. A quick VAR check proves so.

Surely there is another goal in this one? It is a surprise there has not been since Garcia got a goal back for Fulham.

The latest booking of the game goes the way of Castagne, who cynically trips Colwill.

Sessegnon is played in down the left channel and flicks it past Acheampong inside the Chelsea penalty area. Sessegnon gets his shot away from a narrow angle and it is straight at Sanchez.

Palmer looks like he might have cramp in his calf and is going to be replaced by Estevao. Quenda also comes on for Chelsea, coming on for Rogers.

Robinson just has to lift it over Sanchez from the edge of the box but his effort goes wide. Fulham should be on level terms.

Fulham fans think they are about to be awarded a free-kick right outside the box but instead the free-kick goes the other way. It was a clear dive from Bassey, who is rightly booked for simulation.

James is the third Chelsea player into the book for cynically pulling King back. James then has the cheek to wag his finger at King, as if it was not a foul, yet it was a clear booking. James had to be careful there as some referees may not have taken too kindly to that.

Double change for Fulham as Kevin and Sessegnon are brought on.

That would have been a great goal from King. He has already scored once and is inches away from his second. He receives a pass on the turn from Robinson and drives towards the Chelsea box. This is a very open, end-to-end game and you would fully expect more goals in this one. I would be very surprised if this one ended 3-2. Both defences are looking leaky.

Fulham are going to make their substitution of the night as Charles comes on for his debut having signed from Southampton, replacing Bobb.

Enzo is being booed a lot by the home fans every time he touches the ball.

Chelsea are the first to turn to their bench. Enzo is coming on and is met by a lot of boos, mostly though from the home fans as the majority of the travelling Chelsea fans are applauding him. Chavarria is also on to make his Chelsea debut. Hato and Lavia head off.

There is a new rule being implemented. Hato takes far too long over a throw-in and Fulham are therefore awarded the throw-in instead.

When Palmer put Chelsea 3-1 up, the visitors looked in control of this match. Fast forward five minutes and the momentum has completely switched around. What an absorbing opening Monday night of the season!

The Fulham debutant gives them life and this game is not over. Castagne is found making a run in behind and cuts back inside onto his left inside the Chelsea penalty area. His shot is straight at Sanchez, who can only parry it straight into the path of Garcia, who heads into the ground and the ball bounces over Sanchez into the Chelsea net. As he gets to the Fulham penalty area, he waits for the overlapping run of Palmer and times the pass just right. Palmer, from a narrow angle, puts it between Leno’s legs and into the far corner.

Nottingham Forest are ramping up their pursuit of Chelsea’s Liam Delap as Oliver Glasner eyes two major signings before the window closes.

An absorbing first half at Craven Cottage is brought to a close and Chelsea take a 2-1 lead into the break. Pedro put them ahead inside the first minute before King equalised for Fulham. However Rogers, on his Chelsea debut, put the visitors back in front not long before half-time.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Palmer, who has run the show for Chelsea in this first half, is inches away from putting the visitors 3-1 up. Both sides have been guilty of giving the ball away in dangerous areas and Fulham do so on this occasion. Palmer then curls an effort from the edge of the box but his shot goes just wide of the far post.

The British record transfer puts Chelsea back in front on his official debut. It stems from great play from centre-back Lacroix, who finds himself in an advanced position and receives a pass from Palmer on the right side of the box. Lacroix cuts it across to Rogers, who makes no mistake from 12 yards out. Assist and goal both coming from new signings.

A goal for Morgan Rogers on his Chelsea debut! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/hphe8y077v

Fulham fail to clear a cross from James into their box and Hato’s header falls at the feet of Lavia, whose shot from close range is saved by Leno.

Is Colwill lucky to still be on the pitch? The ball is played in behind the Chelsea defence and Colwill appeared to throw his arm across King but no foul is given. That could so easily have been given as a free-kick and a second yellow card.

Rogers drives towards the Fulham box and cuts inside onto his right foot. His effort is blocked by Cuenca before James’ first-time shot is straight at Leno.

Chelsea are inches from going back in front. It stems from great work from Palmer, who drives down Chelsea’s right. His cross from the right side of the box picks out Pedro near the penalty spot. The Brazilian volleys it first time but his effort goes just wide.

Fulham are on top at the moment and Chelsea are lucky shaky as they are under the cosh inside their own box. King is playing really well, finding pockets of space down Fulham’s right and looking a real threat.

Fulham are back on level terms but it is really poor goalkeeping from Sanchez. King, who had just threatened down Fulham’s right, receives a pass from Castagne on the right touchline and takes a touch into the Chelsea box. King then fires his shot away at the near post and gets plenty of power on it but there is no way Sanchez should be beaten. He is beaten and Fulham equalise. Chelsea haven’t spent all that money on Rogers for his defending, but Alonso won’t have liked the way he let Josh King to run past him to collect the ball and smash Fulham level. Rogers switched off there.

Fulham are flirting with danger in and around their box and are a touch fortunate not to concede a second goal.

Down the other end, King is urged to shoot from outside the box and he obliges. Palmer had just one Premier League assist to his name throughout last season and has already matched that tally tonight on the opening weekend.

Colwill is booked and is perhaps a touch fortunate, although what saved him is that you perhaps could not definitively say that it was a denial of a goal-scoring opportunity.

Two former Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain teammates go head-to-head in the dugouts at Craven Cottage as Fulham host Chelsea in a west London derby to round out the opening weekend of the new Premier League season. Alvaro Arbeloa and Xabi Alonso were teammates at Liverpool, Real Madrid and Spain and both had stints as Real Madrid manager last season but have new homes in London. Arbeloa has replaced Marco Silva, who is now at Benfica, whilst Alonso is Liam Rosenior’s permanent replacement. This is the first time a manager’s Premier League debut has come against someone he also played alongside in the competition.

“I know Alonso well because I have watched so many games of his teams,” Arbeloa said. “We have to be ready, and if we want to beat them we will have to play very well. I spoke to Xabi a few days ago. But not about football; both of our families are coming to London, and we are very good friends, until Monday night [tonight]. We will be there on the touchline, so close for 90 minutes, and we will give everything for our clubs. For those 90 minutes, we are not friends.”

Arbeloa has gone back to his former club to add a couple of players in the shape of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios. The opening weekend has not served Fulham well of late; they have won just one of their last six Premier League opening weekend fixtures. They concluded their pre-season with a 1-0 win over Stuttgart.

Chelsea have been very active in the transfer market this summer, breaking the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as adding experience through the likes of Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck, whilst the likes of Marc Cucurella, Andrey Santos and Trevoh Chalobah have moved on. They finished off their pre-season with a 3-1 victory over Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge just over a week ago.

“We feel ready,” Alonso said. “We have prepared the whole pre-season with some players from the first day, other ones coming later, but the desire, the ambition, the hunger to start the Premier League is already in the building each training [session] and we are looking forward to it.”

Enzo Fernandez has been strongly linked with a move away this summer, with Manchester City’s interest well-known.

“Enzo is a Chelsea player,” Alonso added. “He is a top, top player. He is training really well since he started 10 days ago with the team, very integrated. We are happy with him and he is getting ready for Monday. He is training really well, good attitude and that is what we want. He is trying his best to prepare for the kick-off of the Premier League.”

These sides finished on the same number of points (52) last season, with Chelsea finishing ahead on goal difference. It was one win apiece for each club in the two Premier League meetings last season. Nearly a year ago, Chelsea won 2-0 at Stamford Bridge whilst Fulham won 2-1 in this fixture at Craven Cottage back in January. Chelsea have won six of the past eight Premier League meetings at Craven Cottage.

#1656. Man City face £35m French goalkeeper demand as Liverpool and Man United join race

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 18:48

Manchester City are reportedly preparing a £26m move for Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, but the Premier League giants face a significant financial obstacle as Liverpool and Manchester United also monitor the highly-rated French international.

The 21-year-old has emerged as one of the most sought-after young goalkeepers in European football following his rapid development at Lens, where he established himself as first choice after arriving from Strasbourg in the summer of 2025.

According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch, City are leading the interest in Risser and have been scouting him for some time, with a potential offer of €30m (£26m) under consideration ahead of next summer's transfer window.

However, Lens are reportedly demanding at least €40m (£35m) for the France international, who remains under contract until June 2030.

Liverpool and Manchester United are also keeping close tabs on his situation, while Italian giants Inter Milan and Juventus have joined the list of potential suitors.

Risser's emergence represents a remarkable piece of recruitment by Lens, who paid Strasbourg just €3m (£2.6m), plus potential bonuses, to secure his signature in July 2025.

The former Red Star loanee quickly established himself under Pierre Sage, helping Lens finish second in Ligue 1 and win their first Coupe de France during the 2025-26 campaign.

His performances also earned him a place in Didier Deschamps's France squad for the 2026 World Cup, although he has yet to make his senior international debut.

New national team manager Zinedine Zidane has retained faith in the youngster, selecting him for November's Nations League fixtures against Italy and Turkey.

At 6ft 4in, Risser possesses the physical attributes expected of a modern goalkeeper, combining an imposing aerial presence with composure in possession and the ability to initiate attacks from the back.

Those qualities have reportedly attracted Manchester City's attention, although the proposed transfer fee could complicate their pursuit.

Lens have another financial consideration when assessing potential offers, as Strasbourg negotiated a sell-on clause when Risser moved between the two Ligue 1 clubs.

While 4-4-2.ch reports that Strasbourg would receive 25% of any future transfer fee, French newspaper L'Equipe previously described the clause as 25% of the profit generated by a subsequent sale.

The precise terms have not been publicly confirmed, but the arrangement would reduce the amount Lens could retain from a major transfer.

That provides additional context for their reported £35m asking price, which would represent an enormous increase on the goalkeeper's original acquisition cost.

Despite his growing reputation, Risser has experienced a considerably more difficult start to the current campaign.

Lens have conceded 31 goals in 15 matches across all competitions, including a humiliating 9-1 Champions League defeat against Como earlier this month.

Nevertheless, his international recognition and long-term potential appear to have maintained the interest of several leading European clubs.

Manchester City's reported interest is particularly intriguing given the presence of Gianluigi Donnarumma, who remains the established first-choice goalkeeper under Enzo Maresca.

The Italian international has been a key figure since joining from Paris Saint-Germain, meaning Risser would face considerable competition for regular opportunities if he moved to the Etihad Stadium.

Any potential deal could therefore be viewed as a long-term investment, although there is currently no suggestion that City are planning to replace Donnarumma.

Liverpool's interest raises a different question, with uncertainty surrounding the long-term future of Alisson Becker potentially encouraging the Reds to assess younger alternatives.

The Brazilian has remained an important figure at Anfield, but Risser's age and experience in both Ligue 1 and the Champions League make him an attractive prospect for clubs planning beyond their current number ones.

Manchester United are also understood to be monitoring the Frenchman despite already having Senne Lammens in their squad.

Neither Liverpool nor United have been reported to have submitted a formal offer, and their interest remains at the monitoring stage.

Risser has previously attracted attention from other Premier League clubs, with Newcastle United making initial contact with his representatives in March.

Tottenham Hotspur were also linked with the goalkeeper earlier this year as they considered alternatives to Guglielmo Vicario.

The latest reports suggest that Lens could face a considerably more competitive market for Risser next summer, with Inter and Juventus providing additional interest from Serie A.

For Manchester City, the immediate issue is whether they are prepared to meet Lens's £35m valuation or negotiate a lower fee for a goalkeeper whose contract still has more than three years remaining.

With the French club under no immediate pressure to sell, their reported asking price may prove the decisive obstacle to any deal.

#1655. The virtues of patience

It’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

It was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

This was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

By then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

Come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

The Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he says he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he said, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, says the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

“The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

“Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”

To be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and new faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

Ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.

#1654. Emotional Massaro pays tribute to Baresi: “Every day it’s harder and harder”

Daniele Massaro has spoken about how much Franco Baresi meant to him, and how much he now misses the AC Milan icon.

The incredibly sad news broke over the summer that Baresi had passed away following a battle with illness. Thousands of fans lined the streets to pay tribute at his funeral, while the club have honoured him in several ways, including in the first home game against Venezia.

Given his importance to Milan both as a player and then as an ambassador, it has left a huge hole in the hearts of many, above all his former team-mates and colleagues who shared a dressing room and/or an office with him for many years.

At the presentation of Mauro Suma’s book ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’ many former players spoke, including Daniele Massaro. He was visibly emotional during his speech, admitting it is actually getting harder to arrive at work each day and not have Baresi there.

#1653. How Arsenal have evolved in 2026-27

There was a lot of speculation as to how Arsenal might change this season having flung a 22-year-old monkey (how long do monkeys live for?!) from their back in May by finally winning a league title. Would lifting the Premier League trophy lead to a new era of more expressive, urbane football?

I always had my doubts, not least because your style of play is always defined by your talent. Most of Arsenal’s elite talent is behind the ball. Arteta didn’t build Arsenal from the defence first, in my view, because he felt specifically that was the best way. It was just the area of the team that required the most attention when he was appointed.

In attacking areas, he had talent, even if it wasn’t balanced. Aubameyang, Lacazette and Pepe with Saka and Martinelli coming to the boil was a good collection of talent, even if the pieces didn’t always fit neatly together. The list of defenders he inherited included Mustafi, Sokratis, Holding, Chambers, Kolasinac and Mari. That’s why he went defence first, broadly speaking.

The moves the club have tried to make in recent seasons, especially this summer, shows you that Arteta wants his attack to be sharper than it is. For reasons I won’t relitigate here, the club were not able to add a number of high end attacking targets. Which means once again, Arsenal are reliant on Arteta’s coaching talents to squeeze more juice from the orange. Here are three things that have jumped out at me this season.

Arsenal spent a lot of money on Bruno Guimaraes this season and I will come onto some of the reasons why in the next section. But that signing has given Arteta a deep well of central options, with Rice, Bruno, Lewis Skelly, Odegaard, Merino and Zubimendi part of this midfield menagerie.

Arsenal use these options interchangeably and often according to game state. Art de Roche of the Athletic went into how Arteta has used the divergent profiles of Myles Lewis Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes so far in this campaign. In home games against Leeds and Everton, Lewis Skelly got the nod from the start.

In away games at Nottingham Forest and Liverpool, Bruno’s more robust approach was favoured. The pair have made significant impacts from the bench too. When the 1-0 victory at Anfield had become a little too ‘basketball’, Lewis Skelly came on and provided calm assurance in possession.

When the Gunners needed a little more belligerence away at Sunderland, Bruno came on and larruped the ball into the top corner from 25 yards. However, Arteta didn’t part with a significant part of his summer budget for a 28-year-old (he turns 29 next week but, for now, he remains 28 because that’s how it works) to be a high level rotation option.

Against Hull City last weekend, Bruno was selected and he played deeper than Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard. As Adrian Clarke pointed out in his match analysis piece, Bruno passed the ball to Odegaard 25 times in that match and the pair exchanged 35 passes in total. The idea was clear, to use Bruno’s punchiness in possession a little lower to feed Odegaard.

Against Everton, Mikel Merino was selected in midfield and Lewis Skelly started at left-back. I think this was about more than mere rotation. Arteta always highly respects the aerial capabilities of David Moyes’ Everton team, which makes sense since he played in a David Moyes Everton team for such a long time.

In 2023-24, Arteta selected Fabio Vieira ahead of Kai Havertz in midfield at Goodison Park because he wanted to keep the ball on the floor (Arsenal won that game 1-0 via a short corner routine because they did not see the logic of aerial corners against a team like Everton).

Last season at the Hill Dickinson Arsenal enjoyed a season high for passes attempted and completed because they wanted to keep the ball on the floor and avoid transitions. Arteta has a carousel available to him in midfield and a different club in the bag depending on what is called for on the day.

Per Opta, Arsenal have been caught offside 35 times so far this season, at least 11 more times than any other team. That rate of 3.5 offsides per game is the highest of any Premier League team since 2009. Kai Havertz has been flagged 15 times now, the next highest offender in the league is Dominic Calvert-Lewin with eight. Opta provide a deeper dive on those numbers here.

So what does this tell us, aside from the fact that Havertz needs to work on his timing? It means that Arsenal are far more willing to go in behind and they are willing to test the opposition backline earlier in moves. This was a big part of the reason they signed Bruno in the first place, Arteta wants to play with the risk reward dial with the ball.

Havertz also hasn’t been quite good enough to finish some of those one v one situations when he has got in behind the opponent’s back line. He fluffed his lines against Hull last weekend and in the 3-0 defeat at Brighton, he blasted his effort straight at the Brighton keeper when put through one v one.

But here, I will express my usual caveat, we need to normalise strikers missing chances and focus more on process than outcome. Most chances are missed, you want to worry when your striker is getting few shots. There have also been nascent signs that Arsenal have been using Gyokeres well in some of these situations.

That Havertz chance at the Amex was created by Gyokeres taking one touch with his back to goal and hooking the ball past the committed defensive line. Gyokeres did much the same for Madueke in Prague. It seems like Arsenal have worked on getting Gyokeres to use his physicality to initially retain the ball- something he badly struggled with last season- but creating situations where he can release it quickly.

Arsenal’s out of possession prowess is one thing that has been a constant from last season. It is Arsenal’s superpower, so even when they can only manage one goal, it is usually enough to take maximum points. To retain their superpower, Arsenal changed to stay the same, if that makes sense.

The signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa was questioned by many but his presence has made the absence of a world class centre-back like William Saliba a sidebar, which is quite a feat. Arsenal ostensibly took William Saliba’s pizza chart and looked for the most Saliba like defender they could find and bought Konsa.

The loss of Saliba ought to have offered an enormous threat to Arsenal’s defensive stability. Arsenal’s tactical organisation out of possession is elite but so too are the individuals that helm it. Raya, Saliba, Gabriel and Rice are among the best players in the world in their respective positions.

Taking out one of those pillars ought to have derailed Arsenal’s defensive stability and it hasn’t because Konsa has the quality and poise to retain the team’s biggest strength. His pass completion stats are Saliba-esque and the quality of not giving the ball away needlessly is a significant part of the Gunners’ meanness.

How much Arsenal could improve in attack without significant additions was an unknown so Arteta could not afford to sacrifice the team’s defensive ceiling while he plays with those levers. The addition of Konsa was a personnel change that allowed Arsenal to remain the same.

#1652. A Yeboah back in the Premier League? Leeds legend Tony's nephew Kelvin wanted by several clubs in January transfer window after scoring 18 goals in MLS for Minnesota United this term

Published: 04:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 04:36 EST, 11 November 2026

Another goal-packed season for Kelvin Yeboah in Major League Soccer (MLS) is expected to spark interest among Premier League and Championship clubs in January.

Yeboah has ended the campaign with 18 goals and made five assists for Minnesota United who finished 10th of 15 teams in the Western Conference, just one point outside and one place outside the play-offs.

It means the season is over for the 26-year-old nephew of Leeds legend Tony Yeboah.

Yeboah describes himself as 'more of a modern nine' than his uncle Tony, who was famed for his muscular physique and his ability to strike with ferocious volleys from distance. He is sharp and mobile with a goal instinct.

Premier League and Championship clubs have been monitoring his progress this season.

Everton and Crystal Palace, both in search of firepower and options up front, are among those who have been linked to a move. Free-spending Ipswich are another.

Kelvin Yeboah is wanted by many Premier League goals after a fine goalscoring season in MLS

Yeboah scored 18 goals for Minnesota United - with Everton, Crystal Palace and Ipswich keen

The striker is the 26-year-old nephew of Tony Yeboah, a Leeds United legend of the mid-1990s

There is interest also from Europe. Hoffenheim boss Christian Ilzer signed Yeboah when in charge of Sturm Graz, after the young forward had scored four goals against his Austria Vienna team in a cup tie in the previous season.

Yeboah has been in Minnesota since the summer of 2024. There is another season on his contract and the option of one more after that.

But he remains keen to test himself at the top of the European game and there is a growing feeling that he could be on the move in the next window.

'As a footballer, you want to play on the biggest stages and express who you are as a person,' he told Daily Mail Sport in an interview on the eve of the MLS season. 'I just want to keep scoring goals and give myself the best chance of that happening.'

He grew up in Italy from the age of three to 15 and represented the Azzurri at Under-21 level. He is also eligible for Ghana where he was born.

At 15, he moved to London where he played non-league football for AC London and had trials at several clubs including West Ham before joining WSG Tirol in Austria at the age of 18.

Yeboah scored 20 goals in a year at Sturm Graz before returning to Italy. He was 21 when Genoa signed him for £6million. It should have been the perfect homecoming but the club then owned by 777 Partners plunged into financial chaos.

Relegated from Serie A they were unable to pay wages and Yeboah was loaned to three different clubs in three different countries before finding stability in Minnesota. He has 36 MLS goals in 79 appearances.

#1651. "Best team in the world" Spain will have too much for England in fascinating Nations League affair

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 19:17, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 19:21

Ahead of Spain's UEFA Nations League clash with England on Sunday, Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law discusses La Roja's chances of success.

It's an outstanding team. March 2024 was the last time they lost. They did lose to Portugal in the Nations League final on penalties, but technically that counts as a draw, so it doesn't work against them in terms of this record.

They are just the outstanding team in the world, let alone Europe, and the clear number one in world football at the moment.

That win the other night against Czechia epitomised everything that they could do without their best player, and without Oyarzabal, who's been fantastic for them.

Laporte and Rodri were missing too. But they put a team on the field, and you look at the team and you say, "It's a really good team."

On paper, they had Yeremy Pino and Alex Baena, Fermin Lopez and Ferran Torres, and don't get me wrong, these are wonderful players, but it's not Kylian Mbappe, it's not Lamine Yamal, it's not Harry Kane.

Those forwards are not at the top of world football. But as a team, they get the job done.

They didn't really have to break sweat in that 2-0 win on Thursday, which put them on five wins from five in the section. It's an outstanding team, and one that will be strengthened by Lamine Yamal. He had a slight knee injury.

I wonder how much of an injury it was, or whether, after that Barcelona-Atletico game, they just decided to give him a bit of a rest for the Czechia game because they felt like they could win without him.

He's coming back into the squad, and Luis de la Fuente said that he's in excellent shape for this game, so I'm fully expecting him to come back into the starting side.

Oyarzabal had an illness and also stayed behind for the birth of his second child, so he will join up with the squad as well.

He's a player I really like and someone I've watched a lot of in La Liga. He's had an excellent record for Spain, with 31 goals and 12 assists in only 64 games, which is really good.

He hasn't had the best start to the season for Real Sociedad, no doubt about that. He has been a little bit off it, in that it took a while for him to find the back of the net for them, but his international record is outstanding.

Lamine Yamal has 25 goal contributions in 16 games for Barcelona this season, and 11 goals and 14 assists in 37 games for Spain. So we all know what to expect from Lamine Yamal in this game. Interestingly enough, will Nico Williams come back in?

He missed out the other night through illness, and it's still unclear whether he is going to be available or whether he's going to be on the bench. Laporte was also ill the other night.

That's my point, really: they can miss these players. They're one of those international teams where you can make four, five or six changes. The pattern is so embedded in what they play, the brand of football, through the youth team and through the training sessions.

The quality obviously drops when you haven't got those top players, but the patterns of play are still the same. The players still know what they're doing.

It's generally going to be good enough to beat most other teams. I don't think Spain with an under-strength team would fancy their chances against the best teams, but in 90% of the games they play, if they put their second string out, they're going to win. That's just how it is. It's an interesting game.

I did the England post-match piece for Sports Mole last night, and I said that was not a performance that would leave the likes of Spain quaking in their boots for this game.

I think Spain are the big favourites, especially considering the players that they'll welcome back in and their form. The manager's outstanding, and what an international manager he has turned out to be for Spain.

It's a tough game for England. Topping the group from an English point of view would be great, but it was always about getting through to the next round.

It would have been a disaster really if England didn't manage to make it through. Spain were always going to be the favourites to top the group.

They're the favourites for the Nations League, and they're probably going to be the favourites for the next Euros and the next World Cup. That's just the way it is. Zubimendi was an interesting one for me the other night.

He's going through a difficult spell club-wise at Arsenal at the moment, but he was one of Spain's best players last time out.

Pedro Porro has had his problems at Tottenham, but on the international stage he turns into Cafu when he's playing for Spain.

He was outstanding at the World Cup. Cucurella, and Cubarsi has gone to a new level with Spain and with Barcelona as well. They're good defensively.

Rodri is missing, but Fabian Ruiz has been excellent this season for PSG, and he's always excellent for Spain.

Someone else I did just want to mention, lastly, is Alex Baena, who had his chance at the World Cup with Nico Williams having his fitness problems.

He has five goals and four assists this season for Atletico Madrid, and he caused Man United all sorts of problems when they played against him in the Champions League.

He's an outstanding wide technical player, 25 years of age. If Nico Williams can't play, then he is some player off the left for them as well.

So there are worrying signs. If I'm honest, I do think Spain win this game, but I think it'll be relatively close, just like the last game was.

It was a really good spectacle last time out between these two sides. But Spain are the best team in the world at the moment. I expect them to win this, top the group and, to be honest, I expect them to win the Nations League as well this year.

#1650. Building in Barca and the Jim Reaper strikes again

Greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

Of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

#1648. An Arseblog update

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a plan for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very big way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

#1647. Thomas Tuchel responds to Morgan Rogers' Cole Palmer defence

By Naim Beneddra | 13 Nov 2026 19:44

England manager Thomas Tuchel has responded to Morgan Rogers' passionate defence of Cole Palmer after the Chelsea midfielder branded suggestions that his teammate lacks commitment to the national team "a lie".

Rogers spoke out following England's 2-1 Nations League victory over Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, a result that secured the Three Lions' place in the quarter-finals of the competition.

The 24-year-old, who opened the scoring against Croatia, dismissed claims that Palmer does not want to represent his country, insisting that the Chelsea playmaker's recent international absences have been related to managing his fitness.

Palmer was omitted from Tuchel's latest squad despite featuring regularly for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso this season, having previously withdrawn from international duty because of injury concerns.

The England manager had suggested that Palmer was missing too many opportunities to impress, prompting further questions about the 24-year-old's standing within the national team.

However, when Rogers' comments were put to Tuchel after the Croatia victory, the German appeared unconcerned by his player's public intervention.

Speaking at his post-match press conference, Tuchel made it clear that he had no issue with Rogers defending his Chelsea teammate and long-time friend.

"It's totally fine. He's his team-mate and I guess his friend, so why wouldn't he?" Tuchel told reporters.

The England boss explained that he had not heard the full interview and therefore did not wish to comment directly on its contents.

Instead, he praised Rogers' contribution against Croatia, highlighting the commitment he had demonstrated throughout the encounter.

"I think he was the standout player today, offensively and defensively, and that's what matters," Tuchel added.

Rogers had earlier delivered an emphatic response when asked about the suggestion that Palmer was reluctant to play for England.

"It's a lie. He wants to be here," Rogers told BBC Radio 5 Live, before explaining that the midfielder had been eager to receive another international call-up.

The two players have known each other since their time in Manchester City's academy and are now teammates at both Chelsea and international level.

Rogers revealed that Palmer had endured a particularly difficult period with injuries last season and had struggled to feel fully comfortable on the pitch.

The former Aston Villa attacker argued that carefully managing those physical problems was necessary to protect Palmer's long-term career.

He also expressed frustration that the player's absence had been interpreted as evidence of insufficient dedication to England, rather than a decision influenced by his fitness.

Rogers hopes Palmer will return to international duty in the near future, believing his quality would be a significant asset to Tuchel's squad.

Despite Rogers' intervention, Palmer still faces a difficult challenge in establishing himself as a regular member of Tuchel's England squad.

The Chelsea attacker was overlooked for the 2026 World Cup following an injury-disrupted campaign and has made only three appearances for England since Tuchel took charge in January 2025.

His absence from the November squad was particularly notable because he has returned to regular club football, recording five goals and three assists in his opening 11 appearances of the 2026-27 season.

When explaining his decision to leave Palmer out of the squad earlier this month, Tuchel acknowledged the midfielder's desire to represent England but stressed the importance of being available during international camps.

The German also pointed to the strength of his attacking options, with Jude Bellingham, Eberechi Eze, Rogers and Fulham youngster Josh King all competing for opportunities in advanced positions.

Palmer's situation has already attracted support from Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, who previously defended the decision to withdraw from international duty when the midfielder was experiencing physical discomfort.

Tuchel has insisted that the door remains open for Palmer, although his selection decisions suggest that availability and involvement in training camps will remain important considerations.

England will complete their Nations League group campaign against Spain in Madrid on Sunday, November 15, having already secured qualification for the quarter-finals.

Palmer will again be absent, leaving Tuchel with another opportunity to assess the attacking players currently ahead of him in the international pecking order.

Rogers, meanwhile, strengthened his own case for further involvement with his performance against Croatia, earning particular praise from the manager whose selection policy he was indirectly questioning.

#1646. Romano and Moretto provide update on Milan’s Endrick pursuit: “Hasn’t said no”

This week, there have been some interesting rumours about AC Milan and their pursuit of Endrick. However, it may have been a bit misleading.

Yesterday, it seemed that Milan were almost out of the race to sign Endrick, with the Brazilian against the club’s Devil logo. Instead, the Corriere dello Sport report would have you believe that he’d prefer a move to Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, his agency have denied this rumour and later reports suggested that the Rossoneri are very much in the race to sign the Brazilian. In fact, he could even leave Real Madrid permanently – with future clauses – so things have certainly developed a bit this week.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Romano provided an update on Endrick’s situation alongside Matteo Moretto and their words have been relayed by MilanNews.

“Endrick is currently evaluating his future. On one side, Real Madrid doesn’t want to release him, from the president to Jose Mourinho, who continues to reiterate this publicly; on the other, the boy wants to play,” Romano started.

“I wanted to add a footnote: Endrick’s entourage, ROC Nation, are letting it be known that the player hasn’t said no to Milan; he hasn’t said no to anyone on November 12th. He’s still in the evaluation phase; we’ll see what happens.

“He has two months left with Real Madrid: football changes in five minutes. Endrick’s position is currently completely open, and he’s a player—we were the first to talk about him—that Milan really likes. But it’s true that Roma is also there, there’s a queue of many teams ready to chase him.

“I just wanted to clarify that Endrick hasn’t said no to Milan. He’s keeping everything open while waiting to figure out—if he leaves—the best solution.”

Moretto then added, “A lot will depend on the player. In December, he’ll really understand what kind of path he wants to take. He’s currently noticing this lack of playing time, so the loan option is taking shape. Roma have been maintaining contact for weeks.

“Roma want an additional striker because they believe with one or two signings they can really compete for something important this year. Keep an eye on Roma, but Milan was one of the first to move, and the relationship between Cardinale and ROC Nation is excellent. So far, Roma has maintained contact a little more actively, but Milan is insisting.”

It’s clear that January will be very interesting where Endrick is involved, especially with him being the one to make the decisions on his future.

#1645. Croatia vs Czech Republic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 13 Nov 2026 20:04, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 20:07

Croatia and Czech Republic will round off their respective UEFA Nations League Group A3 campaigns with a clash on Sunday night.

The home team will enter the match off the back of a 2-1 loss to England, while Czech Republic were beaten 2-0 by Spain in their last fixture.

A record of one win and four defeats has brought Croatia three points in Group A3, with the national team currently sitting third in the table.

The Checkered Ones cannot qualify for the quarter-finals of the competition and are instead bidding to finish third ahead of Czech Republic.

Slaven Bilic's side will claim third if they avoid defeat on Sunday, and they will be determined to finish what has been a disappointing Nations League campaign on a positive note.

Croatia opened their Group A3 campaign with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic, but they have since been beaten twice by both Spain and England.

The Checkered Ones are actually unbeaten against Czech Republic, winning four and drawing three of their previous seven matches with Sunday's opponents.

Czech Republic had no answer to Spain's class on Thursday, and the Representatives are at the bottom of Group A3 on zero points from five matches.

Santi Denia's side opened their campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Croatia, before losing twice to both England and Spain, and it has been a tough Nations League campaign for them.

Czech Republic will finish fourth unless they are able to overcome Croatia.

The Representatives last played in League B in 2024-25, but they are facing relegation to that stage for the next Nations League campaign.

Denia's side have only managed to find the back of the net twice in their five matches, with a lack of a reliable goalscorer proving to be incredibly problematic.

Croatia have no players suspended for this match, and they will welcome Ivan Perisic back into their squad, with the experienced attacker serving a ban against England.

Luka Modric could be introduced into the starting side, having featured off the bench last time out, with the 41-year-old in line to win his 208th cap.

Ante Budimir is an option in the final third of the field, but the expectation is that Igor Matanovic will continue through the middle for the home side.

Czech Republic, meanwhile, will be missing Ladislav Krejci, with the centre-back picking up his second red card of this Nations League against Spain.

Adam Hlozek has scored five times in 51 appearances for his country, and the 24-year-old is expected to continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be an introduction into the team for the experienced Tomas Soucek.

Livakovic; Smolcic, Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol; Modric, Kovacic; Sucic, Baturina, Vlasic; Matanovic

Kovar; Coufal, Zima, Vicek, Jurasek; Kral, Soucek; Ambros, Hlozek, Provod; Naderi

Both teams have struggled in this Nations League campaign, and we are expecting Sunday's match to be close in terms of the scoreline, but Croatia should be able to navigate their way to their second win in the section.

#1644. Finland vs San Marino - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 13 Nov 2026 21:47, Last updated: 14 Nov 2026 16:35

Finland will conclude their Nations League C campaign on Sunday, when they welcome San Marino to Bolt Arena.

The hosts come into the final clash of the group stage in third place with seven points, while the visitors are last in fourth with no points, and neither can secure promotion.

Finland are certain of their place in Nations League C in the next iteration of the competition, but because second-placed Belarus have 10 points and boast a better head-to-head record, the highest they can finish is third.

The hosts' hopes of promotion ended when they lost 2-0 against Albania on November 12, which was their second consecutive defeat.

It was also the third time in four games that they failed to score, though they have only conceded four goals in the group stage so far.

Head coach Jacob Friis deserves credit for his team's resilience at home given they have won four, drawn one and lost just one of their last six outings as hosts.

Finland kept two clean sheets in those six home clashes, while they did not concede more than one goal in any of those matches.

San Marino would have been relegated in previous editions of the Nations League, but Nations League D will not exist from 2028-29, meaning they cannot be demoted.

It would be wrong to suggest the visitors have improved in any meaningful way, but after conceding 10 goals in their opening three group matches, conceding four times in their next two clashes could be seen as a small step in the right direction.

Manager Roberto Cevoli was in the dugout when his team were beaten 7-0 by Finland on September 26, and another loss this weekend would be his country's eighth consecutive defeat against their hosts.

The visitors' have failed to win any of their last 20 fixtures in all competitions, with the nation only earning one draw in that period, and a defeat on Sunday would extend their losing streak to eight games.

San Marino have also lost each of their 10 most recent away trips, a stretch in which they scored just five goals.

Finland have two players suspended for Sunday's match, with centre-back Miro Tenho having been sent off against Albania, while midfielder Adam Markhiev has now accumulated too many yellow cards.

Robert Ivanov came on in defence late in the game against Albania, and he can be expected to partner Tony Miettinen on Sunday.

In the middle of the pitch, Anssi Suhonen may be selected to feature alongside Kaan Kairinen and Leo Walta.

San Marino will hope that central defenders Marco Pasolini and Dante Rossi can protect shot-stopper Edoardo Colombo.

Fausto Salicioni is yet to find the back of the net in seven appearances for the national team, but he could be given another chance to impress alongside Nicola Nanni.

Filippo Fabbri picked up his second yellow card of the tournament last time out and must now serve a one-game ban.

Hradecky; Stahl, Miettinen, Ivanov, Lahteenmaki; Kairinen, Suhonen, Walta; Svanback, Pohjanpalo, Hakans

Colombo; Benvenuti, Pasolini, Rossi, Giocondi; Meloni, Della Balda, Capicchioni, Zannoni; Salicioni, Nanni

There is no reason to think that San Marino can pull off a miraculous victory and defy their Nations League form.

Finland may be disappointed about their failure to earn promotion, but against a team as porous as the visitors, anything other than a comfortable home win would be surprising.

It seems AC Milan will not be signing Nicolo Tresoldi in January, with Club Brugge making a statement to the press.

In recent weeks, if not longer, Milan have been constantly linked with signing Tresoldi. A fan of the club, the German-Italian striker is an obvious candidate to make a move to San Siro in the near future, especially with Gerry Cardinale being a big fan.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, the finances of the deal make it difficult to really imagine it happening in January, after the Rossoneri paid €75 million for Goncalo Ramos in the summer. Now, a new obstacle has emerged and it’s both financial and literal.

This afternoon, MilanVibes have relayed a statement from Club Brugge, published in the popular Belgian paper Het Laatste Nieuws, saying that the striker will not be leaing in January. Indeed, despite the interest from the Diavolo and clubs from the Premier League, he will not be sold, even if bids of €60-70m arrive.

At €60-70m, a deal feels extreme, but pushing €80m feels like a step too far for the striker…

#1642. Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”

Forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

“For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

“We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

The 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C

Aug 29: Liverpool vs Nottingham ForestSep 5: Nottingham Forest vs Tottenham HotspurSep 12: Aston Villa vs Nottingham ForestSep 19: Nottingham Forest vs CoventryOct 11: Crystal Palace vs Nottingham Forest
